title: Commanders fire tight ends coach following DWI arrest
content:
LEESBURG, Va. — The Washington Commanders announced the firing of tight ends coach Ben Steele on Monday following his recent arrest on suspicion of driving while intoxicated in Virginia.

The move comes just two days before the start of training camp.

According to court records, Steele was pulled over for a traffic infraction of changing course after signal. In addition to the DWI, Steele is also facing charges for refusing a chemical breath or blood test as well as obstructing or resisting an officer without force.

The three charges — DWI, refusing testing and obstruction/resisting arrest — are all class 1 misdemeanors in Virginia. A first-offense DWI is punishable by up to 12 months in jail, a fine ranging from $250 to $2,500 and a one-year driver’s license suspension.

The Commanders placed Steele on leave after he informed them of his arrest, and the team reported it to the league, according to a source with knowledge of the situation but not permitted to speak publicly about the situation. Steele was later fired because of a violation of a team policy.

Commanders offensive assistant Wes Welker coached the tight ends during mandatory minicamp in June while Steele was on administrative leave.

The NFL declined to comment, and Steele’s attorney did not immediately respond when contacted by email.

This story will be updated.
